comments.value: Note: the third attachment (output_log_success_excerpt) is a 2.8 KB excerpt of the full 741 KB successful log; Canny rejected the full file. The complete log is available on request.

Additional diagnostic checks were performed after the initial report and are attached: crash dump locations, Visual C++ redistributables, Defender settings and Windows updates. All results are clean, with one notable finding — after 10+ reproductions there is no crash dump anywhere on the system, which suggests the game exits gracefully when SteamAPI_Init fails rather than hard-crashing.

details:
After updating to build 1938 (2026.4.1p2-1938-565822d00a-Release, Steam buildid 26551832, installed 2026-11-13 01:21), VRChat crashes ~4 seconds after launch when started via Steam / EAC. Before this update it ran fine (1900+ hours on this account).

The engine loads (process reaches ~1180 MB, ~89 threads, EAC confirms the game window became visible), then the process exits. No crash dump is produced. Every output_log stops at:

[SteamManager] Initializing Steam API for AppID

438100...

The next line a healthy session prints ("initialized Steam connection - AppID: 438100") never appears. Crash logs are 511-599 bytes; a normal session log on this machine is 58 KB - 1 MB.

Launching VRChat.exe directly, WITHOUT EAC, on the same install and driver works completely: 741 KB log, Steam login succeeds, rendering normal (AMD Radeon RX 6750 GRE 10GB / Direct3D 11 level 11.1 / 10194 MB), main loop entered. The only error is the expected "[AntiCheatClient] Anti-cheat client not available". So Steamworks initializes fine outside EAC and fails inside it, on identical binaries.

EAC itself reports nothing wrong: "Launcher finished with: 301, Easy Anti-Cheat successfully loaded in game", game window became visible, "Terminating with: 0". The kernel driver EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys is signature Valid (Epic Games Inc., valid until 2029-02-02) and the System event log shows a clean FilterManager load/register and unload each attempt. A full EAC uninstall + reinstall (runtime module redownloaded from CDN, HTTP 200) changed nothing. Adding steam_appid.txt (438100) only changes the AppID source line to "Overriding Steam App ID to 438100 from steam_appid.txt" — the crash is byte-for-byte identical, so it is SteamAPI_Init itself failing under EAC, not AppID resolution.

Already ruled out (each tested individually, none changed the crash): file integrity verified twice; Steam overlay off; Steam game recording off; GameDVR/GameBar off; Logitech G HUB closed; --no-vr launch; GPU driver (0 display-driver timeout events in 14 days); memory integrity / HVCI off; Tencent ACE anti-cheat not running (all drivers Stopped/Manual, 0 processes); Defender controlled folder access and network protection off; no mod loaders or injected DLLs (MelonLoader, BepInEx, version.dll, winhttp.dll, winmm.dll all absent); CmUpx.sys absent; Steam restarted and also tried as administrator.

Reproduction steps:

1. Launch VRChat via Steam. EAC splash appears.

2. Game window appears ~3 seconds later (confirmed in EAC's own log).

3. Process reaches ~1180 MB, then closes ~4 seconds after the window appears.

4. output_log_*.txt is 511-599 bytes and ends at "438100...".

5. Repeat: happens on every attempt (10+ times today).

Environment: Windows 10 Home 10.0.19045, Intel i5-12400F, 32 GB RAM, AMD Radeon RX 6750 GRE 10GB (driver 32.0.21045.16010, 2026-10-16), 1920x1080 @ 180 Hz. EAC product id a4a57ff548934dbeba0cc7c62cdf9f34.

Attached: two crash logs (511 B and 599 B), one successful no-EAC session log (741 KB), and anticheatlauncher.log.
title: VRChat crashes during SteamAPI_Init under EAC (build 1938); direct launch works
